title: What the compiler and the JVM decide about primitives

questions.stem: Per this page, which types can a plain `switch` in Java 21 take as its selector?

options.says: The page leaves long out: only char, byte, short and int are accepted.
Those four and their wrappers are exactly what the page says a plain switch still accepts.
The page says patterns over other primitives arrive only as a Java 23 preview.

questions.stem: Per this page, in which situation is a type such as `Integer` the right choice over `int`?

options.text: In a performance-critical loop that runs millions of times
options.says: The page says to use primitives in performance-critical code.

options.text: In a large array that must use as little memory as it can
options.says: The page says wrapper objects take more memory and to prefer primitive arrays.

options.text: Inside a generic collection, or where null must be allowed
options.says: Generic collections and a valid null are the two cases the page gives.
